I don't know if I really buy the whole argument that colonizing other solar systems (or even other galaxies) would really "ensure survival" of the human race. It would very likely increase the chances of short term survival. However many if not all of the long term potential threats to our survival here on Earth would be just as relevant in other solar systems. The real truth of the matter is that with our current technology and understanding of physics, the human species is doomed long term no matter what. The universe is doomed. Either heat death or the big rip or some other un-survivable fate is almost certainly the ultimate result for this universe we inhabit.

The true ultimate survival of humanity will require either developing god-like technology such as time travel or the ability to create wormholes/travel to other universes/create new universes/etc. Learning how to fly to Alpha Centauri or even the Andromeda galaxy and colonize it/build a home for humans there/etc. is nothing more than a delaying of the inevitable fate we have coming here at home. Keeping Earth safe seems kind of a minor concern in comparison when you consider that every single source of power in the observable universe is going to eventually disappear. Imagine living in a reality where you look up at both the day sky and night sky and both are pitch black. Not a fun place to call home.

I think colonizing other places in the future is a fun idea in the same way that going to the Moon in the 60's was a fun idea, but it's also similar in that it doesn't accomplish a huge amount of practical gain beyond the cultural/political/social significance. It's something we do to prove that we can rather than because we NEED to.
